r_lead: SOSistem™ detects within seconds a person on the floor, an earthquake, a gas leak or a violent situation in restrooms, changing rooms, cabins and confined spaces, with no cameras and no recording, and escalates the alert all the way to 911.
r_prob: Every year 684,000 people die from falls and 37.3 million falls require medical attention (WHO, 2021). Nearly 3 million people die from work-related causes (ILO, 2023). Where law and dignity rule out cameras, an emergency can go unnoticed for critical minutes.
r_sol: Imageless sensors (mmWave radar, gas, smoke, oxygen, sound and vibration) and terminals that report instantly. The alert escalates by level to the person in charge, the monitoring centre and 911 with a CAP message, and the equipment runs for up to 30 days without grid power.
r_esc: 82 % of people aged 10 and over own a mobile phone (ITU, 2025): every phone can be a sensor, a screen or both. In Mexico alone there are 258,522 schools (SEP, 2025) and 17.7 million people aged 60 and over (INEGI, 2026).
r_ali: Contributes to SDGs 3, 8.8 and 11.5, to target (g) of the Sendai Framework and to the “Early Warnings for All” initiative (see chapter 7). Where early warning is limited, disaster mortality is nearly six times higher (UNDRR and WMO, 2024).
r_dif: Only states and measurements; no images, video or voice recording.
Tiered N0–N3 alert; immediate upon a confirmed fall or an earthquake.
Light, sound, 22 languages, braille, Morse and sign language.
Battery of up to 30 days; works with or without a network.
From one person's phone to an entire building, a city or a port.

cel_lead: Mobile phones, tablets, computers and other devices, online or offline, can work as sensors, as observation and information terminals (screens), or as both at once.
cel_imp: Anyone can download SOSistem™ to their phone, activate it and link it to a family member 24 hours a day, 7 days a week: upon a fall, upon the words “S.O.S.” or “help”, or when the system itself detects the fall, the family member is alerted instantly. With 82 % of people aged 10 and over owning a mobile phone (ITU, 2025), protection can reach billions of people without installing a single device.
cel_imp_b: No video, voice or conversations are recorded: it is only real-time help.
cel_como: Download and activate SOSistem™, no sign-up required.
Link with a family member using the same phrase on both devices, only once.
Detect the fall, the words for help or immobility, even if the person cannot touch the screen.
Alert instantly the family member; if no one responds, the alert escalates to 911.
Cancel by voice: “all good” stops a false alarm.
cel_sens_cel: Accelerometer (fall and impact), gyroscope (rotation and tilt), microphone (recognizes only “S.O.S.”, “help”, “it's shaking” and “all good”; it does not record), location with permission, immobility and pocket mode.
cel_sens_fij: mmWave radar, motion, distance, sound level, smoke, gas, oxygen, hydrogen, ammonia, heat, cold, light and darkness, water on the floor, mass, space and capacity, people count and dwell times.
cel_estado: Status: the phone Terminal is available as a public test version, with voice always active and phone-to-screen linking by phrase; the permanent 24/7 family link is under development.
cel_foto: “Person on the floor” test with N0–N3 alert
acc_lead: In an emergency, not everyone can hear, see or speak. SOSistem™ delivers every alert through four complementary channels so that alerts and help reach everyone.
acc_br_t: Braille: how to call for help without seeing the screen (proposal)
acc_br: Braille plate next to each terminal and in the cabins, with the word “SOS” and directions to the help button.
Raised tactile button: holding it down for 3 seconds sends the alert, even if the person cannot see or speak.
Vibration and sound confirmation: a pattern felt in the hand indicates that help has been alerted; useful for blind or deafblind people.
On the phone: alert with a gesture (triple tap) and reading via VoiceOver or TalkBack; the user's braille display shows the alert status.
acc_br_n: Proposal under development; it will be validated with blind, deaf and deafblind people and their organizations.
